categories: Needs a human (visual / mobile / UAT wording)
statusMessage:
code-review: fail-pending-Q22 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q22, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

So lengthening retention under a hospital affiliation would change what the purge keeps but not what either timeline shows. This goes against UAT 3.6 ("all windows are configuration values"). The oracle says such a window is a finding that becomes a Fail or a pass only once Q15 decides whether the displayed window must follow the config. Both findings are therefore labelled pending:Q15 and the verdict is pending. No recorded gap applies.

NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

statusMessage:
code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Fail. The Vertex mapper, toVertexConvexError, copies the first line of the provider's error message (up to 300 characters) into ConvexError data.detail (vertex.ts:135). invokeVision throws it on any failure (vertex.ts:168). Both vision()'s runWithRetry (retry.ts:183) and the aiAction wrapper (phi.ts:191-196) pass it on unchanged. ConvexError data always reaches the client, so the photo scans (scanCensusSheet, scanClinicSchedule, scanPriorNote) hand provider-controlled text to the browser. Google error lines name resource paths such as projects/<id>/locations/..., so a project ID can get through, and so can a service-account email or a sentinel if the provider message holds one. The OpenAI batch transcription path also forwards OpenAI's own error.message (apiErrorMessage, openai.ts:19; transcribe.ts:162). An OpenAI 401 echoes a partly masked sk-proj key, and the comment at openai.ts:6-7 says this text is meant to reach the physician. That one is a plain Error, which Convex normally hides from clients on production deployments, so it reaches the client on dev and preview, and on production only if that hiding is off. The Specode email relay does the same with the relay's payload.error (email.ts:42-47), under the same caveat. Clean paths: Bedrock sends only the kind, error name and HTTP status (bedrockErrors.ts:92); SES sends only the HTTP status (ses.ts:123); the live-session path sends fixed text plus the HTTP status (transcribe.ts:105-106). No recorded gap or open question a…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): When a photo scan (census sheet, clinic schedule or prior note) fails at Vertex, the browser receives Google's raw error line in the error data. That line can contain the Google Cloud project ID and, in IAM denials, a service-account email, both of which are visible in the network traffic or devtools. On non-production deployments, a failed recorded-audio transcription can also show OpenAI's error text, which can include a partly masked API key. / When a census, schedule or prior-note photo scan fails on Vertex, Google's own error text (which can name the service-account email or the GCP project) is sent to the physician's browser or phone. The client may also show it in an error toast. On a dev deployment, OpenAI and email-relay error text can reach the client the same way.

statusMessage:
code-review: known-gap → known gap (known gap)
No. At e02167f a Nursing Home resident has no facility field anywhere in the chain. The snf resident record (snfFields in convex/lib/validators.ts, which convex/schema.ts spreads into snfResidents) holds name, age, dob, sex, mrn, unit and so on, but no facility. snf:add takes exactly those fields as its args, so the mutation can't accept a facility either. The Add Resident form asks only for Full Name, Date of Birth, Unit / Room and MRN, plus Encounter Type. SnfPatientCard builds its identity line from unit, dob, age and mrn. matchesPatientSearch matches on name, room, unit, mrn and diagnosis. A case-insensitive search for 'facility' under apps/web finds only prompt text, billing labels and comments, never a data field. This is exactly the recorded gap known:no-facility. As the oracle says, U4's facility part and U6's facility field are a Fail on TFA-92581, not Blocked or not-built, and that holds whatever Q1 decides about where facility comes from. No open question is waiting on this, and the question's pass/fail rule agrees with the Then/Oracle.

statusMessage:
code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

The server holds OPENAI_API_KEY and mints a client secret that lasts 60 s. The browser then POSTs its SDP offer to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with that secret, and the audio goes straight to OpenAI over WebRTC. It is authenticated but does not pass through our server. (2) 'gpt-live', recovery of a kept recording: the recording is uploaded to the authenticated `transcribeAudio` action, which sends it to whisper-1 at https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions from the server. (3) 'whisper', or no row (`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION = "whisper"`): `prepareSession` returns batch mode, and audio is uploaded through Convex to whisper-1 from the server. (4) 'voxtral', 'transcribe', 'transcribe-medical': `transcriptionRoute` throws in its default branch, both in `prepareSession` and in `transcribeAudio`. These values are refused and nothing falls back to OpenAI.
